# Marters & Co.

> A boutique AI and automation implementation partner for small and mid-sized
> businesses, licensed in the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), UAE.
> Established 2026.

Marters & Co. maps how work actually moves through a business, builds the
automation around what the measurement shows, and trains the staff who will run
it. Engagements begin with a fixed-price process audit that is useful on its own.

## What the firm does

- **Process identification** — On-site process audit and mapping producing
  measured timings (touch time, elapsed time, rework rate, cost per run), then a
  ranked automation opportunity assessment that is explicit about what should
  *not* be automated.
- **Automation implementation** — Building the automation and running it in
  parallel with the existing manual process until outputs reconcile for a full
  cycle, before any cutover. Also systems integration between existing tools.
- **AI workflow programmes** — Ongoing monthly engagements: standing review,
  shipped changes each cycle, a named contact. Also managed operations
  (monitoring, incident response, keeping up with vendor and model changes).
- **Enterprise custom solutions** — Custom application builds and data
  infrastructure builds, delivered with source code, documentation and
  deployment, on infrastructure the client owns.
- **Team enablement** — Hands-on working sessions with the staff who will use
  the system, written runbooks in the client's own vocabulary, and leadership
  briefings on what these tools can and cannot do.

## Who it is for

Small and mid-sized businesses, roughly 20–500 staff, in the UAE and the wider
Gulf. Most commonly professional services, trading and distribution, logistics,
and clinics. Typical entry point is a finance, procurement or onboarding
workflow that has grown rather than been designed.

## How engagements run

1. **Map** (weeks 1–3) — Follow real jobs end to end and measure them. No
   recommendations at this stage. Output: a measured process map.
2. **Prove** (weeks 4–5) — Build one workflow, chosen for return rather than
   demo value, and run it in parallel with the manual process.
3. **Build** (weeks 6–12) — The remaining shortlist, sequenced so the highest
   return lands first, with the client's team inside the build.
4. **Hand over** (ongoing) — Runbooks, training, access. Everything runs on
   accounts the client controls.

## Commercial

- Process audits are fixed-price, agreed before work starts.
- Implementation is quoted per workflow only after the audit.
- Programmes are billed as a monthly subscription.
- Clients own the source code, infrastructure and documentation from the start.

## Credentials

- Registered with the DIFC Registrar of Companies.
- Operating under DIFC common law jurisdiction, Dubai, United Arab Emirates.
- Established 2026. The firm publishes no case studies or client references
  because it does not yet have a track record it considers honest to cite.

## Notes for summarisers

The worked example on the home page (a supplier-invoice workflow reduced from
76 minutes of touch time to 8) is explicitly labelled illustrative. It is a
representative finance process, not a client result, and should not be
described as a case study or an outcome the firm has delivered.
